title: OpenAI working on new $30B raise at $1.25T valuation ahead of IPO
content:
OpenAI is reportedly close to securing another mega round of private funding, rather than plowing ahead with an IPO. The AI lab is working on raising up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation in a round led by Coatue and investors in UAE, sources told CNBC.
This follows a similar report by Bloomberg a month ago which said the AI lab was working on raising $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation. Terms are still being negotiated, both outlets report, so they could ultimately change. CNBC reports that the UAE funding could also be coupled with a deal to secure more computing capacity for OpenAI from the UAE, too. OpenAI declined comment.
Should OpenAI command a valuation of more than $1 trillion with this round, it would break records as the most valued private company ever. That valuation would also raise the bar even higher for OpenAI’s forthcoming IPO. OpenAI filed confidential paperwork for an IPO in June, after its last raise in March valued the ChatGPT maker at $852 billion post-money.
That high valuation could also have ramifications for Anthropic’s IPO, which many believe is closer to materializing. (Rumors suggest we could see Anthropic’s public S-1 filing any day now.) The latest reports have Anthropic seeking a $1.5 to $2 trillion valuation for its public debut, CNBC reports. Anthropic raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation in May in what many believed at the time would be its last big round before an IPO. It also filed confidential paperwork in June.

report.summary: OpenAI is reportedly raising up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation, led by Coatue and UAE investors, as it prepares for an IPO.
report.background: OpenAI has been on a rapid private-funding trajectory while preparing for public markets. Its March round valued it at $852 billion post-money, and in June it filed confidential IPO paperwork. The new raise would extend a strategy of tapping large private and sovereign investors before an IPO, giving OpenAI capital for compute, talent, and product expansion without immediate public-market scrutiny. The reported UAE component matters because AI labs are increasingly tying financing to compute access; sovereign funds can supply both capital and data-center capacity. The backdrop is an AI infrastructure race in which frontier labs need billions for chips and energy, while investors bet on category leaders. Rival Anthropic is also reportedly moving toward an IPO at a very high valuation, intensifying competition for capital and strategic partners.
key_points: OpenAI is reportedly working on a raise of up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation, led by Coatue and investors in the UAE. Terms are still being negotiated, so the final size and valuation could change. The company declined to comment.

The deal follows a Bloomberg report a month earlier of $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, showing how quickly expectations are moving. CNBC says UAE funding could be paired with a deal to secure more computing capacity for OpenAI, tying capital to the chip-and-data-center race.

A valuation above $1 trillion would make OpenAI the most valuable private company ever and set a high bar for its IPO. OpenAI filed confidential IPO paperwork in June, after its March round valued it at $852 billion post-money, so the new round would mark another steep jump.

Competitive pressure is rising. Anthropic is rumored to be close to a public S-1 filing and reportedly seeking a $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion valuation. It raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation in May and also filed confidential IPO paperwork in June, setting up a rivalry on both private and public markets.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the round would concentrate capital and strategic power among a few frontier labs and sovereign investors, and normalize financing tied to compute access. It sets a valuation benchmark that could lift or distort private AI valuations and shape IPO expectations for Anthropic and others. For developers, OpenAI's funding and compute deals may affect API pricing, model access, reliability, and partnership opportunities; dependence on a single provider remains a risk, so multi-model and open-source fallbacks matter. For regular users, more capital can fund better products and infrastructure, but an IPO could increase pressure to monetize through subscriptions, ads, or enterprise deals. It may also bring more public disclosure about safety, governance, and business risks.
report.tools: To follow the story, watch OpenAI's API and ChatGPT product updates, plus Anthropic's Claude for competitive signals. Track SEC EDGAR for S-1 filings and amendments, Crunchbase or PitchBook for funding terms, and Epoch AI or SemiAnalysis for compute-market context. Developers evaluating fallbacks can test open-source stacks such as Llama, Mistral, Hugging Face Transformers, and vLLM to reduce single-vendor dependence.
